incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas (≈9,000 K-12 districts and universities; ~275M individuals)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing and social engineering of staff via Free-For-Teacher accounts gave the attackers repeated access to Canvas back-end systems, including a second intrusion after Instructure claimed containment.
incidents.impact: Roughly 3.65TB of names, emails, student ID numbers and billions of private messages from ~9,000 institutions stolen; defacements forced Canvas offline mid-finals across major U.S. universities and K-12 districts; Instructure suspended Free-For-Teacher accounts and notified FBI/CISA.

incidents.victim: NYC Public Schools (one Manhattan campus computer lab)
incidents.vector: Malware installed on shared computer-lab machines at a Manhattan school community, discovered amid the broader Canvas outage.
incidents.impact: Malware was removed and the district is investigating with local police; no further disclosure of data loss or attribution yet.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal agency software contractor (45+ federal agencies including EEOC)
incidents.vector: Two fired contractor employees (Sohaib and Muneem Akhter) used stolen credentials to access protected federal databases without authorization after termination.
incidents.impact: Sohaib Akhter convicted on federal computer-fraud and identity charges for deleting 96 government databases and destroying evidence; he faces up to 21 years in prison.

incidents.vector: Researcher (LayerX) found Claude's Chrome extension allowed any other browser extension — even without special permissions — to inject hidden instructions and hijack the AI agent across Google Drive, Gmail and GitHub.
incidents.impact: Demonstrated exfiltration of Drive files, surveillance of email, and theft of private GitHub source code; Anthropic shipped only a partial fix on May 6 and the researcher still bypassed it in some scenarios.

incidents.victim: Microsoft customers (SharePoint, Defender, Chrome, Adobe Reader)
incidents.vector: May Patch Tuesday addressed 167 Microsoft CVEs, including SharePoint zero-day CVE-2026-32201 (spoof/social-engineering, under active exploitation) and Windows Defender flaw 'BlueHammer'; Chrome and Adobe Reader also patched actively exploited zero-days.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation of the SharePoint flaw enables phishing and impersonation inside trusted SharePoint environments; risk extends to any internet-facing SharePoint deployment until patched.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer-overflow zero-day CVE-2026-0300 in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication (Captive) Portal allows remote code execution as root; attackers injected shellcode into the nginx worker and used SAML floods to fail over to a second device.
incidents.impact: Limited but confirmed exploitation; post-compromise activity included EarthWorm/ReverseSocks5 tunnelers, Active Directory enumeration with stolen firewall service-account credentials, and systematic log wiping.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools (AVB Disc Soft) users — selected government, scientific, manufacturing and retail orgs in Russia, Belarus and Thailand
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised AVB Disc Soft's build/signing pipeline and shipped backdoored DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate from at least April 8; selected victims received a second-stage QUIC RAT.
incidents.impact: Thousands of infections; targeted deployment of QUIC RAT against ~12 high-value organizations for likely espionage; pattern matches prior Chinese-speaking-actor supply-chain operations (CCleaner 2017, Notepad++ 2025).

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source-code repository; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Trellix says it has no evidence the build/release pipeline or shipped source was tampered with; concerns remain that stolen source code may reveal detection logic and control locations, giving attackers a roadmap to evade Trellix products downstream.

incidents.victim: DigiCert (certificate authority) and ~27 downstream EV code-signing customers
incidents.vector: Social engineering: attacker posed as a customer and tricked two DigiCert tech-support staff into running a malicious .SCR (Windows screensaver) file; one CrowdStrike EDR agent was misconfigured and not reporting, letting the attacker dwell for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: 27 EV code-signing certificates stolen and used to sign Zhong Stealer payloads (linked to Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog/APT-Q-27); all 60 in-flight EV orders revoked and customer initialization codes exposed.

incidents.vector: Sustained DDoS-for-hire attacks by pro-Palestinian hacktivist group 'The 313 Team' against Ubuntu and Canonical domains and APIs.
incidents.impact: Multi-day outages of Ubuntu install/update infrastructure; users globally unable to install or patch the OS; same group previously hit BlueSky and Mastodon.

incidents.victim: cPanel/WHM-hosted websites (44,000+ systems including Guam government sites)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of cPanel/WHM authentication-bypass CVE-2026-41940 (patched 30 April) to take over shared-hosting sites; attackers wipe pages and post fake $8,000 Bitcoin ransom demands, deploy cryptominers, and recruit servers into DDoS botnets.
incidents.impact: Per Shadowserver Foundation, more than 44,000 cPanel systems compromised; Guam government sites taken offline; Australian Cyber Security Centre issued a critical alert and confirmed active exploitation in Australia.

incidents.victim: Cuba's embassy in Washington, D.C., plus 5,000+ Microsoft Exchange servers globally
incidents.vector: Chinese hackers compromised a Microsoft Exchange email server at Cuba's embassy and stole diplomat mailboxes, as part of a wider campaign hitting 5,000+ Exchange servers worldwide.
incidents.impact: Targeted theft of Cuban diplomatic correspondence around U.S. naval blockade activity; broader campaign indicates large-scale Exchange compromise still active in 2026.

incidents.vector: Unattributed intrusion into the national healthcare database; Moldovan cyber officials say Russian involvement cannot be excluded but no ransom was demanded.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial data on nearly every adult Moldovan and on all CNAM-affiliated private medical providers stolen; ~30% of the database was either stolen or had to be restored from backup; payments to providers continued uninterrupted.

incidents.victim: Linux endpoints across virtually all major distributions since 2017
incidents.vector: 'Copy Fail' (CVE-2026-31431): deterministic local-privilege-escalation logic flaw in the Linux kernel's algif_aead crypto module; a 732-byte Python script reliably overwrites the page-cache of setuid binaries (su/sudo) to gain root without modifying anything on disk.
incidents.impact: Affects Ubuntu, RHEL, Debian, SUSE, Amazon Linux, AlmaLinux on kernels 4.14–6.19.12; bypasses file-integrity tooling; enables Kubernetes container escape, multi-tenant host takeover, and CI/CD pipeline compromise. Patches available; immediate kernel updates strongly urged.

incidents.vector: Intrusions into operational technology at five water-treatment stations across Poland during 2025; some attackers reached industrial control systems.
incidents.impact: Polish intelligence service (ABW) confirmed the incidents but did not attribute them to any foreign state; underscores ongoing OT-targeting risk for water/wastewater operators across NATO-adjacent states.

incidents.victim: Itron (U.S. utility metering / grid technology vendor)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into Itron's internal corporate systems; entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Itron says the incident has been resolved and that cyber insurance will cover most costs; given Itron's footprint across U.S. utilities, downstream exposure for grid/metering customers warrants follow-up.
